Halloway Books Adds Audio Editions

By Simone Achterberg

PRESTWICK (October 8)—Halloway Books, an independent publisher known for its
mystery novels, announced last week that it will begin releasing audio versions of its
titles. The first five audiobooks will be available in November, and the company plans
to add about two titles each month after that.

Until now, Halloway has sold the audio rights to its books to larger companies. "Those
deals brought in money, but we had no say in how the books were read," said
publisher Darren Moyo. "Now we can choose the narrators ourselves."

The recordings are being produced at a studio the company built on the second floor
of its Prestwick office. Several Halloway authors have agreed to narrate their own
books. Others will be read by professional actors.

The audiobooks will be sold through the company's Web site and major online stores.
Customers who buy a print copy directly from Halloway will be able to purchase the
audio edition for half price.
